title: Chief of Staff
description:
Overview 

Physical AI, a real model of the world, is the next trillion dollar opportunity and a foundational pillar for energy, robotics and superintelligence. 

At Jua we are building it now. Our models already run on four continents and help power the energy buildout needed to support ever larger intelligence. 

We are assembling a world-class team of researchers and entrepreneurial minds to turn this model into reality at global scale. If you want the opportunity of your life, come build physical AI with us.

The Role 

You work directly with Jua’s Leadership. You operate as a force multiplier — plugging into whatever's highest-leverage that day, from fundraising and investor work to product calls, deals, and fixing what's broken before it slows us down. What you're pulled into will shift as the business does — some stretches this is heavily fundraising and investor-facing, others it's operational firefighting or unsticking a cross-functional project. The pace is high, the context load is real, and you'll see everything. This is also a launchpad into an executive leadership role.

This role is best suited for someone who has been an early-stage operator or ex-founder, and has hands-on experience with start-ups that are still in the build-phase. If that's you, expect a founder's vantage point on how Jua scales — the pace and stakes of building it yourself, without carrying it alone.

What You Will Do 

- Problem-solve directly with the leadership team on the highest-leverage issues across the business — from product, marketing and operations to fundraising and partnerships.

- Sit in high-stakes meetings with customers, investors, and strategic partners, and turn what happens there into clear next steps.

- Bring clarity to priorities and make sure decisions actually turn into action.

- Build lightweight dashboards and operating rhythms that help the team learn from data that's still evolving — without pretending it's cleaner than it is.

- Be the glue across the business: spot where cross-functional work is stuck and personally unblock it — including outside your core areas, whether that's a marketing crunch, a vendor issue, or whatever's fallen through the cracks.

- Write sharp briefs, investor materials, and internal notes.

- Handle practical execution when it matters — travel, schedules, logistics, on-site coordination.

Who You Are 

- A fast learner who can switch contexts without dropping quality — the mix of what you're doing will genuinely change over time, and you're energised by that rather than needing it to settle.

- Real depth in one or two areas, not experience scattered thinly across many — we'd rather see two or three things you've actually driven than a long list of things you've touched.

- Comfortable with data and analytical tools (vibe coding is enough) — precise enough to help the team make calls on metrics that are still taking shape, without waiting for perfect numbers.

- A clear, concise communicator who compresses complexity.

- High ownership and bias toward action.

- Comfortable with ambiguity — figuring things out as you go — and good at building real relationships across the team to get things done through others.

- Challenges directly — firm, honest input with no ego or personal agenda — then backs the CEO's call fully, including the ones that don't pan out.

- Spots problems before anyone else does, and gets ahead of them — not just reactive once something's already stuck.

- A professional background in a leadership position in one of the following domains, along with cross-functional experience in other parts of the business too : Product, Commercial, People and/or Engineering.

- Hands-on experience at an early-stage startup that is still building, still raising — or founder experience — is a strong plus over scale-up experience.

Requirements 

- Zurich-based strongly preferred - either current location or planning to relocate.

- Frequent short-notice travel to the UK, Nordics, US, and Asia.

- Comfortable operating at high speed with fast decision cycles.

- Professional experience, relationships or network relevant to Jua's industry and customer base preferred.

At Jua, we foster a performance culture and value people who embody our beliefs of service and adventure. We prioritize agility, operating at the highest clock speed to adapt quickly to change. 

We innovate on behalf of our users and leverage data supremacy to maintain our competitive edge. Through clear communication and fact-based decision-making, we ensure alignment in our pursuit of excellence. 

With these principles, we aim to create a customer-focused, value-centric organization that sets new standards in the industry. We value the unique perspectives that each individual brings to the table and believe that embracing diverse backgrounds and experiences enriches our collective journey towards growth and success.

title: Controller
description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry.

Location: 

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

- Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

- The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

- Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

- Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

- Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

- Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

- At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

What you bring

- Experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Senior Accounting Manager at a venture-backed company, with a track record of raising the standard on process rather than just running what exists

- You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it

- Month-end close ownership across two or more legal entities in different currencies

- Deep, hands-on ASC 606, applied to at least one revenue model without clean precedent, and defended to an auditor

- You operate in the detail. You build the calendar, do the reconciliations, and touch the ledger

- Experience developing a small team or a single direct report

Nice to have

- Active CPA license

- Usage-based or consumption billing experience, particularly Tabs, Metronome, Maxio, or similar

- Public accounting background, especially audit

- Software development capitalization under ASC 350-40, including the time capture that makes it auditable

- Experience replacing manual accounting work with automation, and a clear view on what should stay manual

- Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure

- Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure

Benefits

Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere! $1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment. MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs. Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need. Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Apply Today!

Whether you're returning to work after a gap in employment, or taking the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar.

We advance the state of the art in molecular design by training large-scale foundation models that enable cutting-edge generative approaches. Those models learn from diverse biological datasets and are refined through focused experimentation, large-scale training, and feedback from lab measurements. Progress depends not only on building better models, but also on understanding what they learn, where they fail, how data shapes their behavior, and how to evaluate them against biologically meaningful objectives.

You will collaborate closely with AI researchers and biologists to rigorously characterize the behavior, capabilities, and limitations of biological foundation models and their applications. You will identify valuable datasets, develop meaningful evaluations, investigate model behavior, and generate insights that guide model development, data strategy, and experimental priorities across the company.

Your Mission, should you choose to accept it 

- Embody our vision of an antedisciplinary environment and embrace learning about areas outside of your traditional area of expertise

- Investigate how model performance changes with data quantity, data quality, dataset composition, and training methodology

- Develop biologically meaningful evaluations and benchmarks that measure progress toward therapeutic design objectives

- Design and execute rigorous experiments to understand the behavior, capabilities, and limitations of biological foundation models

- Identify sources of potential artifacts, bias, and noise in biological datasets

- Identify promising biological datasets for model training and evaluation, and develop computational pipelines for preprocessing, quality control, and exploratory analysis.

- Design studies, in silico or in the lab, that reveal what models have learned and which biological signals drive model behavior

- Work with biologists to formulate hypotheses and translate biological questions into measurable machine learning experiments

- Partner with AI researchers and engineers to prioritize research directions, data collection efforts, and model improvements

- Analyze, visualize, and communicate experimental findings to inform decisions across teams

Qualifications 

- PhD in computational biology, statistics, physics, machine learning, or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with record of publications or open source tooling in these fields

- Strong quantitative reasoning and statistical intuition

- Demonstrated ability to identify important scientific questions, design rigorous investigations, and draw reliable conclusions from complex biological data.

- Experience analyzing high throughput sequencing data (e.g. RNA-seq, functional genomics / transcriptomics, MPRA), with a focus on robust statistical analysis

- Experience collaborating closely with AI/machine learning researchers or applying machine learning or generative AI tools to scientific problems

- Familiarity with current AI/machine learning methods, including generative foundation models, representation learning, and model evaluation

- Familiarity with publicly available biological datasets and data derived from high throughput assays

- Capable programmer in Python and common scientific computing libraries

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex findings to audiences with diverse technical backgrounds

- Availability to work with team members across US and Europe, with meetings starting at 8am PT and ending at 7pm CET

- Readiness to travel several times a year for company retreats and business events

- We value the benefits of in-person collaboration and expect candidates to primarily work from our office locations

Preferred technical skills 

- 3+ years of post-PhD experience in computational biology, biostatistics, machine learning research, or a related field

Compensation 

$135K – $240K + Bonus + Equity

What we offer

- A competitive compensation package

- 30 days paid vacation per year

- Comprehensive health insurance for US based Beginners

- 401K with company match for US based Beginners and Direktversicherung for German Beginners

- Quarterly company-wide retreats

- Monthly wellness benefit

- Budget for multiple visits per year to our offices in Berlin, Palo Alto or Switzerland

- Learning & Development budget to attend conferences, take courses, or otherwise invest in your professional growth

- A buddy to help you get settled

*Varies by country and does not apply to internships 

At Inceptive, we are creating tools to develop increasingly powerful biological software for the rational design of novel, broadly accessible medicines and biotechnologies previously out of reach. Our team brings together vast expertise in molecular biology, machine learning, and software engineering, and we are all working towards becoming antedisciplinary, meaning we deepen the knowledge we have in our area of expertise while also expanding our knowledge of completely new fields.

We approach our goals with a Beginner's mind, humbly and with fresh eyes, and aim to become the pioneers of a new discipline rooted in biology as much as in deep learning, whose impact will be realized together with out-of-the-box thinkers in business and entrepreneurship, defying established categorizations. We are building a company culture centered around growth, learning, and discovery. We believe in humility and open-mindedness in how we approach each other, as well as problems we don't yet have solutions for.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer
description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 

About the role 

We are looking for a manufacturing quality engineer to own the quality and reliability of the Gravis hardware package that turns regular excavators into awesome, autonomous machines. You will work with our engineering and production team in Zurich defining and implementing quality measures like incoming inspections, supply chain validations, failure analysis and product return teardowns to enable our custom AI hardware a safe and reliable operation of heavy machines. You are capable of working both independently and with others, and are intrinsically driven to solve challenging applied problems with a rigorous attention to detail and an exploratory imagination.

You are our first quality hire. There is no dedicated quality team, no lab, and no playbook; you will design the test / fixture / process and then go build it. 

What you will do 

- Define what hardware quality means for Gravis from ground up

- Design and implement testing systems, jigs and fixtures from incoming inspection to product shipping

- Document failures, root causes and mitigations, build a failure database and review regularly with design and production

- Teardown and analysis of field returns, drive corrective actions

- Own supplier quality: first article inspection, qualification, audits, and 8D follow-through

- Tighten drawings and specifications; critical characteristics, unambiguous acceptance criteria

- Help building our long-term reliability and environmental test strategy as we scale

What we're looking for 

- A university degree in mechanical, electrical, quality Engineering or equivalent practical experience

- 3+ years experience in quality / manufacturing engineering in low volume manufacturing

- Hands on failure analysis and teardowns

- CAD knowledge for designing fixtures

- Experience in hand metrology

- Solid understanding of mechanical and electrical systems

- Good command of English, both written and spoken

Beneficial skills 

- Experience in GD&T

- Experience in SQL / python

- Exposure to environmental / accelerated lifetime testing (e.g. vibration, shock, ingress, UV)

- Fluency in Mandarin

- Off-highway, agricultural, mining or other harsh-environment equipment 

This is an opportunity to join a dynamic, multidisciplinary team and to be part of a company that is reshaping heavy construction.

ID Quantique (IDQ), part of IonQ, is a global leader in quantum-safe communications. The Role: 

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to own the classical cryptography architecture of our post-quantum cryptography (PQC) hardware acceleration products, targeting hardware security module (HSM) and network-appliance applications. Real-world quantum-safe systems are hybrid systems: classical and post-quantum algorithms operating side by side, with careful key management, crypto agility and migration paths. You will be the senior authority for this classical and hybrid layer, working alongside our PQC architecture leadership. The role demands fluency on both sides of the transition: deep classical mastery combined with a solid working command of the post-quantum algorithms and standards the products are built around.

Responsibilities :

You will own the architecture and implementation strategy of the classical cryptographic functions of the product line: symmetric ciphers and modes (AES/GCM and beyond), hash functions (SHA-2/SHA-3, HMAC/KDF constructions), RSA/ECC offload, and true random number generation and entropy architecture (SP 800-90A/B/C). You will define the hybrid classical/post-quantum schemes (key establishment, dual signatures, composite certificates) and the crypto-agility mechanisms that allow customers to migrate safely, track the standardisation of hybrid and composite approaches (NIST guidance, IETF work on hybrid key establishment in TLS 1.3 and IKEv2, composite certificates) together with our PQC architects, guide RTL and software engineers implementing classical cores, technically evaluate third-party IP, and support FIPS 140-3 and CAVP certification of the classical algorithm suite. You will also own key-management and key-hierarchy architecture across the product, ensuring interoperability with deployed HSM, TLS and IPsec ecosystems.

- Own the classical and hybrid cryptography architecture of the product line: symmetric, hash, RSA/ECC, entropy and key management, and classical/PQC hybrid schemes

- Define crypto-agility and migration mechanisms that let customers move to quantum-safe deployments without breaking existing infrastructure

Requirements: 

We are looking for a candidate with a Master’s or PhD in Cryptography, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field and at least twelve years of experience implementing and architecting classical cryptography in real products, in hardware, software or both. You have deep command of symmetric and asymmetric primitives, modes of operation, key management and entropy generation, and you have taken cryptographic subsystems through FIPS 140-3 or Common Criteria evaluation. You also bring a solid working knowledge of the NIST post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) and their deployment constraints: you do not need to be a lattice specialist, but you must be able to architect hybrid schemes with one.

You understand the practical constraints of deployed security infrastructure (HSMs, PKI, TLS and IPsec ecosystems) and how hybrid classical/post-quantum schemes are standardised and deployed in practice. You write precise specifications, guide implementers effectively, and make sound architecture decisions under real-world interoperability constraints. Fluency in English is required; French or German is an advantage.

- Proven architect of classical cryptographic subsystems with certification experience (FIPS 140-3, CAVP, Common Criteria)

- Practical knowledge of hybrid classical/PQC schemes, crypto agility and key-management architecture, with working command of the NIST PQC standards

Preferred Qualifications:

You believe that quantum-safe security is only as strong as the classical foundations it stands on. You enjoy being the guardian of correctness and interoperability in a programme pushing new technology, and you take pride in migrations that customers barely notice because they simply work.

title: Senior Computational Geometry Engineer
description:
SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed.

The Role As a Computational Geometry Engineer, you own the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack - the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model and reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right.
You own the code that runs in the factory.

What We're Looking For - 5+ years building geometry-heavy software in production - CAD/CAM, geometry kernels, feature recognition, CAE/simulation preparation, metrology, or comparable.
- B-rep and Mesh Depth . You think natively in topology and NURBS. Feature recognition, defeaturing, robust booleans, offsetting, surface/surface intersection, healing and repair. You know exactly why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations - and what to do about it. You have had the opportunity to delve into complex CAD models and are able to assess their quality in both quantitative and qualitative terms (gaps in edge, spikes in loops, tiny elements, twisted surfaces...) and ultimately predict which types of processing might be challenged.
- Kernel Fluency . Hands-on with a geometry kernel - Parasolid, OpenCASCADE, ACIS, or equivalent - and the judgment to know which parts can be developed in-house in order to retain full control and IP rights, and which parts too complex (e.g. advanced solvers) should be integrated as 3rd parties. Comfortable with mesh and point-cloud processing (libigl, Open3D, CGAL, PCL) alongside solid modelling.You know well STEP file format and about integration into collaboration & interoperability processes.
- Technical Excellence . Strong command of modern C++ (17+), plus Python for rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write and test performant code. 
- Manufacturing Instinct . Some knowledge of fabrication techniques-casting, stamping, composites, and additive manufacturing-alongside toolsets for evaluating design manufacturability, risk profiles, quality standards, and cost factors.
- End-to-End Ownership . Algorithm design through to a shipped, tested, maintained service.
- First Principles Thinker. You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you know whether the bug is in the code, the model, or the assumption.
- Industrial Grit . You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point.
- Maniacal Urgency . Speed is our only edge. You thrive in the "chaos-to-order" phase of a startup.
- On-site : Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland.

What we're not looking for - Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship.
- CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them.
- Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll go find it.
- People who treat "it works on the test model" as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job.
- Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities.

What we offer - Mission : Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space.

The Role As a Junior Computational Geometry Engineer, you work on the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack: the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model, reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right.
You start on well-scoped parts of that engine, next to the engineers who built it, and grow into owning them. Your code runs in the factory.

title: Product Marketing Manager in Legal Tech (Zurich)
description:
Description Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes. 

You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind. 

Your mission 1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence 

- Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution. 

- Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy. 

- Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters. 

- Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo. 

2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership 

- Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer. 

- Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders). 

- Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice. 

- Own our thought leadership channels, including video, and decide what gets said. Write what can’t be delegated: founder posts, executive bylines, keynote scripts, board-level memos. 

3. Sales & Customer-Facing Enablement 

- Build the sales slides, briefings, one-pagers and competitive battlecards that make Sales and Customer Success more effective in every conversation. 

- Translate positioning and research into materials for specific deals, verticals and executive-level conversations. 

- Work directly with Sales and CS to find out what’s missing in the field. Build case studies and customer proof points that Sales actually uses, not ones that sit in a folder. 

What We Want to Achieve Together 

In 6 months: a flagship study that gets cited by competitors and customers. Sales armed with materials that actually get used in deals. A clear Legartis position that everyone in the company can repeat in 30 seconds. 

In 12 months: Legartis recognized as one of the leading European voices on Legal AI, with a content and enablement engine, you plus the AI tools you direct, that outproduces companies with five times the headcount. 

Your profile - Proven strategist: demonstrated success creating and executing marketing strategies. 

- Storyteller: you craft compelling materials about complex AI products for non-technical audiences. 

- Clear communicator: exceptional written and verbal communication with a strong visual sensibility. 

- Impact-driven: comfortable with experimentation and interpreting both quantitative and qualitative data. 

- AI-savvy: crafty with AI tools and automations — you use them daily and keep exploring what's new. 

- A track record where writing and thinking were central: journalism, industry or analyst research, strategy consulting, or senior product marketing with real strategic ownership. 4+ years in marketing, product marketing or a comparable strategic role at a SaaS company. Classic PMM experience (positioning, GTM, enablement) is a strong plus, not a hard requirement, if your thinking and writing are strong enough. 

- Fluent German and English, executive-level writing in both. 

Why us? - Real editorial ownership over our voice and our position, not a content calendar handed down from someone else. 

- A platform to build your own visible profile as a voice in Legal AI. 

- Modern office in Leipzig or Berlin, hybrid setup, with regular presence in Zürich and team events such as hiking, dinners and offsites. 

- Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) participation. 

- Competitive salary, based on experience and seniority. 

Process - 30 min with our People & Operations Manager: cultural fit, understanding the role and your expectations. 

- Positioning conversation with our Head of Product: bring a point of view on Legal AI and be ready to defend it live. 

- Case study: show us something you’ve written or built, and how you’d turn it into a sales-ready asset. 

- Meet the team in the office. 

- Decision: if it’s mutual, we welcome you to the team! 

How to Apply 

Send us your CV, two or three writing or work samples you’re proud of, and a short note answering: what’s your sharpest point of view on where Legal AI is heading, and what’s the evidence?

title: Senior Robotics Software Engineer - Autonomy Architecture
description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 

About the Job 

The autonomy team at Gravis architects autonomous behaviors for different tasks, e.g. different types of excavation or truck loading. This role owns the architecture that lets those behaviors live in the same software stack as opposed to creating one SW stack per behavior. You'll be responsible for how tasks are decomposed and orchestrated, for the interfaces between, and for the software quality. We are looking for a senior roboticist with C++ and Python expertise and high standards for software quality, who can make clear, pragmatic architectural calls that let the system grow without losing stability.

What you'll do 

Architecture 

- 
Own the task-level architecture shared across our autonomous behaviors

- 
Define clear module boundaries and responsibilities between behavior orchestration, factor out common logic across different tasks

- 
Implement component tests and telemetry/metrics collection pipelines

- 
Identify technical debt early enough to guide the team toward sustainable solutions

- 
Act as the go-to person for software quality: modern C++ practices, code structure, error handling, robustness. Likewise for Python.

Configuration & tooling 

- 
Design an easily extensible and testable module for deploying policies that can be reused across tasks and supports schema versioning for observations, so a deployed policy pins the exact version of the computations it was trained against

- 
Provide technical leadership on C++ and Python tooling (clang-tidy, sanitizers, static analysis, linting, typing, test setup)

- 
Work with our incoming simulation team to unify training, benchmarking and evaluation tooling across tasks, so adding a task doesn't mean forking tooling and infrastructure

What we're looking for 

Required 

- 
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

- 
5+ years developing complex C++ systems, with deep knowledge of modern C++ (17 and onwards)

- 
Strong Python for tooling, configuration and simulation-side scripting

- 
Strong experience designing large, modular software systems that outlived their first use case

- 
High standards for software quality and long-term maintainability

Nice to have 

- 
Experience with behavior trees, state machines, or other task orchestration frameworks in production

- 
Experience working alongside learned controllers in a production stack - deployment, versioning, observation pipelines. No need to train them.

- 
Motion planning, geometric algorithms, or spatial data structures

- 
Feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms

This role is a great fit if…

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Your Impact

Procurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part is not the software, it is that every customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that is where most enterprise AI value quietly dies.

Forward Deployed Engineering is how we close that gap. You sit inside the customer's environment, build in their production data, and turn what you learn there into product. You are one of the first FDEs at Tacto, so you are not slotting into a playbook, you are writing it while shipping in real accounts.

Your Tasks

Build in customer environments. Data pipelines, agents, and custom logic on top of the Tacto platform, in real production data.

Own the technical side of a deployment. Extraction, mapping, validation, enrichment, until the customer's procurement team can actually work with the result.

Be in the room, on site. Run data workshops with key users, debug alongside their IT, and see how a company really buys instead of how the process documentation says it buys.

Turn what you learn at the edge into product. Document the pattern and push it to Product and Engineering instead of quietly rebuilding the same one-off for the next customer.

Automate your own job. If a step in a deployment can be done by an agent, you build the agent and prove it works.

Make it one team. Hold the boundary with Solution Engineering and Customer Value so the customer experiences one Tacto, not three.

Your Profile

- You are a builder. You have shipped software, automations, agents, or technical projects that real users relied on.

- You write code yourself. You are comfortable with Python and SQL and use AI coding tools to move fast.

- You are AI-native. You have built with LLMs against real data and understand where agents work, where they fail, and where humans still matter.

- You thrive in messy environments. Incomplete requirements, undocumented data, and conflicting stakeholder input do not stop you from making progress.

- You can earn customer trust. You explain technical decisions clearly, handle pushback, and do not over-promise.

- You have 0-4 years of experience with evidence of a steep learning curve through strong technical work, ambitious startups, internships, or things you built from zero.

- You speak native-level German and fluent English , are based in Munich, and are willing to travel regularly across DACH.

Why This Role is Awesome

You get to combine building software with seeing exactly how it creates value in the real world. You will ship into production, work directly with industrial customers, and turn what you learn at the edge into product improvements. Do this well for 12 to 18 months and you are among the people who defined what Forward Deployed Engineering means at Tacto, with a direct line into the product roadmap and an obvious next step, whether that is leading a team, going deeper into product, or owning a segment.

What This Role Is, and Isn't

We want to be honest about what you are signing up for.

- This is not an engineering role with customers kept at a safe distance. Customer contact is the job, not a tax on the job. If you want a ticket queue and clean requirements, this is the wrong role.

- This is not consulting. Nobody here bills days. You are measured on what the customer can do afterwards and on what made it into the platform.

- It is deliberately broad. If you want to specialise narrowly you will be frustrated here.

- The deal: prove yourself, deliver real impact, make a strong case for yourself, then we back your next step in every way we can.

Why Tacto

We bet on young talent and mean it. We consistently back smart, hungry, young people with real ownership early. 70%+ of our Leadership Team was promoted internally: you deliver impact and sky is the limit at Tacto.

Backed to win big. We are Sequoia and Index-funded with €50M+ behind us. Our founders sit at the same table as the people defining the global AI agenda. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI.

A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier.

High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring.

A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch & Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Check out all upcoming and past events here: https://luma.com/tacto 

You'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term.

Our Background 

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters 

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI. 

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer 

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

- Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

- Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

- Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.

As an AI Client Executive at supermodular.ai , you will own the development of strategic enterprise relationships and turn complex AI transformation opportunities into meaningful, long-term engagements.

title: Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem
description:
Your mission As our Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem , you will define the product what and why for how ProGlove devices connect, integrate and create value within the enterprise Android ecosystem.

ProGlove is evolving from a wearable scanner company into a Worker Companion company, bringing together ergonomic wearable hardware, software, connectivity, workflow guidance, data and intelligence. With the MAI Wearable Companion, we are entering a broader ecosystem of enterprise applications, technologies, standards, partners and customer infrastructure.

Your mission will be to make our products easy to adopt, integrate and deploy at scale – without turning every customer opportunity into a bespoke engineering project. You will identify recurring customer needs, translate them into scalable capabilities and propositions, and decide where ProGlove should own, enable or partner. In doing so, you will help turn integration from a technical necessity into a source of differentiation, customer value and commercial opportunity.

You will work closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion device. While they own the device proposition, you will own how the device connects to and creates value in the wider ecosystem. Together, you will shape a coherent end-to-end proposition for customers, developers, integrators and partners.

Your day-to-day 
- Define and evolve the product strategy and priorities for ProGlove’s enterprise Android integration and ecosystem capabilities, aligned with customer needs and business goals.
- Work directly with customers, Sales and Solution Architecture to identify recurring problems, distinguish individual requests from broader market needs and turn the right opportunities into scalable solutions.
- Translate recurring integration needs into repeatable product capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, tools, interfaces, documentation, integration patterns and deployment solutions.
- Shape the product experience around device setup, provisioning, application distribution, device management and other capabilities required to deploy and operate connected device fleets at scale.
- Make clear, pragmatic decisions about where ProGlove should own, enable or partner , balancing customer value, strategic control, speed, scalability and technical complexity.
- Identify the platforms, applications, standards and ecosystem players that matter to our customers, and shape the integrations, certifications and technology partnerships that strengthen our proposition.
- Explore where integration capabilities, software, services and ecosystem propositions can create differentiated value and support commercial or recurring-revenue opportunities.
- Partner closely with Engineering and the Product Manager for the Wearable Companion to create alignment on customer problems, priorities, trade-offs and desired outcomes.
- Enable Sales and other customer-facing teams to clearly explain our Android proposition, supported capabilities, integrations and common deployment patterns.
- Maintain a forward-looking view of enterprise Android, AOSP, enterprise mobility, AI and adjacent technologies, and translate relevant developments into strategic options and product priorities.

Your profile At ProGlove, technical expertise matters, but how you work is just as important. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays curious, collaborates openly and turns complexity into clear, pragmatic decisions.

- You bring strong Product Management experience in B2B or enterprise technology and can define strategy, discover meaningful customer problems, prioritize opportunities and turn them into scalable products or propositions.
- You are commercially minded and naturally connect product decisions with customer value, differentiation, business impact and opportunities to capture value.
- You are comfortable working with enterprise software, platforms, connected devices, integrations or technology ecosystems, and understand the realities of complex customer IT environments.
- You have enough technical depth to understand architecture, interfaces and trade-offs, contribute credibly to platform and integration discussions, and recognize when deeper engineering expertise is needed.
- You think in systems and patterns: when faced with a customer requirement, you look beyond the immediate request to understand why it exists, how broadly it applies and what a simple, repeatable solution could look like.
- You take end-to-end ownership, move topics forward without waiting for perfect instructions and remain effective when the product space or path ahead is not yet fully defined.
- You collaborate generously and build trust across Product, Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture, customers and external partners. You can create alignment and drive decisions without relying on formal authority.
- You communicate clearly and transparently, raise risks early and can make complex technical and commercial topics understandable to different audiences.
- You are curious about customers, the business and emerging technologies, and continuously test assumptions rather than pursuing technology for its own sake.
- You use pragmatic judgment to balance speed, simplicity, quality and long-term value.
- You are fluent in English and comfortable working in an international environment.
Experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable, but is not required:

- Enterprise Android, AOSP or adjacent Android ecosystems, including environments operating outside standard Google Mobile Services.
- Enterprise mobility management, MDM/EMM, device provisioning, application deployment or connected fleet management.
- Rugged or industrial devices, IoT or edge devices, connected hardware or other B2B technology ecosystems.
- APIs, SDKs, developer or integrator experiences and enterprise integrations.
- Platform or ecosystem strategy, technology partnerships, certification programs or developer and partner ecosystems.
- Enterprise customers deploying technology at scale.
Direct Android Product Management experience is an advantage, but not essential if you bring strong Product Management expertise and relevant experience from an adjacent enterprise technology ecosystem.

Why us? This is an opportunity to shape an important part of a category that is still being defined. 
Android gives ProGlove access to a much broader technology ecosystem, but the opportunity goes far beyond compatibility. You will help determine what role ProGlove should play in that ecosystem, which capabilities we should own, where we should partner, what customers and developers should be able to build around us, and where integration itself can become a source of differentiation and recurring business value. 
ProGlove already has the customer base, market credibility, technology and industrial expertise to build on. Our products are used in some of the world's most demanding operational environments. What we are now building is the next layer. 
Over time, success will mean more than making our own products easier to integrate. It will mean creating capabilities, interfaces and ecosystem relationships that customers, application providers and partners actively choose to build around - moving ProGlove from ecosystem participant toward ecosystem shaper. 
If you are excited by the idea of turning complex technology ecosystems into simple, valuable products - and helping shape how the next generation of frontline technology connects with the digital world - we would love to meet you. 
Join us in building the future of frontline work.

What success looks like - ProGlove has a clear, customer-backed strategy and prioritized roadmap for Android integration and ecosystem capabilities.
- Recurring customer and integration needs are turned into scalable, repeatable solutions rather than one-off engineering projects.
- Customers can adopt, integrate, deploy and manage ProGlove devices more easily within their existing enterprise environments.
- Decisions about what ProGlove should own, enable or partner are made transparently and based on customer value, business impact and long-term scalability.
- Product, Engineering, Sales and Solution Architecture are aligned on priorities, supported capabilities and key trade-offs.
- Customer-facing teams can confidently communicate our Android proposition and common deployment patterns without relying on Product or Engineering in every opportunity.
- Relevant integrations, partnerships and commercial opportunities are identified, validated and translated into tangible product or business outcomes.

Meet your team You will join our Product team and report directly to the CPO. You will work especially closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion, as well as colleagues across Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture and Product Marketing.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will bring together customer needs, technical realities and commercial opportunities, while also building relationships with external technology partners, platform providers and integrators. The team values open collaboration, clear communication and shared ownership of outcomes.

Defence is a core application of our work today.

We are growing to a team of 100+ people. Join at a stage where you can shape our Perception team , help build the team and grow your responsibilities as the company expands.

You'll work closely with our perception lead, founders and autonomy engineers, shaping architecture and core algorithmic decisions without people-management responsibility. Your work moves from recorded data to field trials and determines how well our platforms understand their surroundings.

- Architecture & Algorithms: Shape the architecture of the perception stack and drive core algorithmic decisions together with the team lead.

- Detection & Tracking: Build object detection and multi-object tracking that stay reliable on real mission data.

- You bring deep expertise across modern perception, including object detection, tracking, segmentation and depth estimation, and you base design decisions on evaluation data.

- You lead through technical influence, setting direction, reviewing designs and helping others grow, without needing a management role.

- You speak fluent English; German is a plus. Given the nature of SE3's work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to work on defence-related projects and, where required, obtain the relevant security clearance.

- Publications at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS or similar venues.

title: Staff Data Engineer
description:
We're seeking a Staff Data Engineer to join one of the fastest-growing AI legal tech companies in Europe. You'll take technical ownership of the data platform behind how we run the business: the pipelines, the warehouse, and the definitions behind the numbers our leadership team actually uses.

You'll report to our Head of Engineering and work alongside a colleague who owns the business-facing side of data, plus our infrastructure and application engineers. This is a senior individual contributor role with no line management in either direction, roughly 70% hands-on building, 30% defining, documenting and explaining.

Your Challenge and Opportunity in This Role 

JUPUS supports hundreds of law firms across Europe, and our customer base is growing roughly 4x a year. Our data platform has grown with it (ClickHouse, dbt, Python extract-load pipelines into an S3 data lake, orchestration in GitHub Actions) and it has grown fast.

Your job is to make it trustworthy. That means modernising what already exists, making historical trends a record of what actually happened rather than a nightly re-derivation of it, and owning the definitions behind the metrics that reach our board. This is not a greenfield build, and it is not a maintenance seat. It is a real platform with real problems, and you would own it.

Tasks 

- Own the data platform end to end: ingestion and the raw layer, the ClickHouse warehouse, and the dbt project on top of it. You're the person who can say whether a number is wrong or the pipeline is.

- Make our numbers trustworthy: reliability, correctness, and a history that holds up, so that a trend is a record of what actually happened rather than a re-derivation of it.

- Own the metrics the company runs on , starting with our customer health score- the definition, the denominator, the eligibility rules and the known limitations, not just the SQL underneath them.

- Turn business questions into durable metrics: work directly with Customer Success, Sales, Product and leadership to understand what they're actually trying to decide, then build something defensible enough to decide on.

- Keep cost and complexity in check as we grow: warehouse architecture, query cost, and the surfaces that deliver data into BI and our CRM. All of it gets harder as the customer base multiplies.

- Set the standard for how data work is done here: one authoritative written definition per leadership-visible number, and the conventions that inform our Data function as it grows with us.

Requirements 

Technical Expertise

- Substantial experience in data engineering or analytics engineering , with production ownership of a warehouse and a transformation layer. We care more about evidence of ownership than about years served.

- ClickHouse in production. 

- dbt at ownership level: incremental models, snapshots, tests, macros, CI/CD. Ideally you've inherited someone else's dbt project and left it better than you found it.

- Python data engineering: EL tooling, S3, CI-based orchestration that you’ve owned end to end, with no platform team behind you.

- Product event streams: PostHog, Amplitude, Segment, Mixpanel or similar. You understand how user-to-company identity and group association break, and what that does to every metric downstream.

Judgement and Ownership

- You have defined a business KPI end to end and defended it to non-technical people. This is the differentiator for us. An excellent engineer who takes requirements as given is not the right fit for this role.

- Analytical rigour: cohorts, correct denominators, sample size stated before findings. You'll say "we can't tell yet, and here's exactly why" rather than produce a confident chart.

- You act without waiting for a ticket , and you can name something you chose to stop doing.

- You're comfortable in front of senior stakeholders , including C-level, and can hold a technical line without losing the room.

Further Requirements

- Nice to have: you're used to non-technical colleagues querying data through AI tools, and you design for that.

🛠️ A Real Platform – ClickHouse and dbt already in production, with genuine problems worth solving. No greenfield theatre, no maintenance seat.

AI is fundamentally changing how enterprises operate.

As AI agents become capable of executing increasingly complex workflows, enterprise customers expect more than presentations—they want to see working solutions inside their own environments.

At Lio, we're building THE AI workforce for procurement. 

As a Sales Engineer , you're not just supporting sales.

You're helping some of the world's largest enterprises understand what's technically possible with AI. You'll build prototypes, lead technical workshops, and work closely with customers to turn complex requirements into working software that proves real business value.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will:

- Build prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and custom solutions that demonstrate the value of our platform

- Configure and adapt Lio's AI platform to customer workflows and enterprise system landscapes

- Lead technical deep dives, live demos, and workshops with procurement, IT, and architecture teams

- Partner closely with Sales throughout the entire enterprise sales process as the technical expert

- Collaborate with Product and Engineering to translate recurring customer needs into scalable product capabilities

- Travel to customer sites for workshops and technical sessions (1–2 times per week)

- Help shape how enterprise customers adopt AI in complex production environments

Your Profile

You'll thrive in this role if you:

- Have experience building software. You're comfortable working with APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, or modern development frameworks.

- Enjoy solving customer problems. You like understanding technical requirements and turning them into working solutions.

- Take ownership by default. You move quickly, build pragmatically, and care about delivering measurable customer value.

- Communicate confidently. You're comfortable presenting technical concepts to engineers, IT teams, and senior stakeholders alike.

- Enjoy working across disciplines. You like collaborating with Sales, Product, Engineering, and customers to make complex projects successful.

- Are curious about AI and excited about bringing cutting-edge technology into enterprise environments.

What's not required

You don't need experience in procurement software or every technology in our stack.

We're much more interested in strong technical fundamentals, curiosity, ownership, and your ability to solve customer problems than in checking every box on a technology list.

Why Join Lio?

Lio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and built at Y Combinator . We're bringing Silicon Valley ambition and speed to Munich while building one of Europe's leading AI companies.

From day one, you'll work with Fortune 500 companies across Europe and the US, helping some of the world's largest enterprises adopt AI. You'll build real solutions, influence our product through customer feedback, and work closely with founders, Sales, Product, and Engineering to shape how enterprise AI is deployed.

If you're excited about combining engineering, customer interaction, and cutting-edge AI, we'd love to hear from you.

Any questions about the role? Feel free to reach out to Cansel .

title: Teamleiter Immobilienverwaltung (m/w/d)
description:
Über Buena 

Buena baut die Technologie, auf der die Immobilienbranche läuft. Wir machen jeden Teil der Immobilienwirtschaft so nahtlos und transparent wie möglich, vom Finden über das Finanzieren bis zum Verwalten.

Dafür übernehmen wir Hausverwaltungen in ganz Deutschland und bauen sie zu Technologieunternehmen um. In den letzten drei Jahren sind wir mit weniger als 30 Leuten im HQ zu Deutschlands zweitgrößtem Immobilienverwalter geworden.

Über die Rolle 

Du kennst den Alltag einer Hausverwaltung und weißt, wie du Ordnung reinbringst, wenn Abläufe stocken, Aufgaben liegen bleiben oder Verantwortlichkeiten unklar sind.

Genau dort setzt du bei Buena an. Jeden Monat übernehmen wir neue Hausverwaltungen, und du überführst sie in den Buena-Betrieb. Deine Basis ist unser Büro in Berlin, deine Einsätze finden in unseren Verwaltungen in ganz Deutschland statt. Dein Erfolg zeigt sich in funktionierenden Abläufen und in Teams, die mit der Buena App besser arbeiten als vorher.

Verantwortlichkeiten 

- Du arbeitest im Tagesgeschäft unserer Verwaltungen mit, erkennst Engpässe früh und baust Rückstände ab. Vor und nach der Umstellung auf die Buena App.

- Du schaffst mit den Teams klare Zuständigkeiten und Prozesse, die auch nach deinem Einsatz Bestand haben.

- Du kennst unsere Software in- und auswendig und trainierst die Teams an ihren konkreten Aufgaben.

- Du bringst deine Erfahrungen aus dem Verwaltungsalltag zurück ins Product-Team. Was du vor Ort siehst, macht unsere App besser.

Du passt gut, wenn du 

- Mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung in der Immobilienverwaltung mitbringst und das Tagesgeschäft eigenständig beherrschst.

- Probleme schnell erkennst, Prioritäten setzt und selbst mit anpackst.

- Klar kommunizierst, schnell Vertrauen aufbaust und Menschen für neue Arbeitsweisen gewinnst.

- Tech-affin bist. Neue Software lernst du schnell und erklärst sie so, dass anderen die Arbeit leichter fällt.

- Bereit bist, regelmäßig bei unseren Verwaltungen in ganz Deutschland vor Ort zu arbeiten, je nach Einsatz auch mehrere Tage am Stück.

- Fließend Deutsch sprichst.

Deine Benefits 

- Bis zu 500 € Close-to-Office-Bonus, wenn du 10 bis 20 Gehminuten vom Büro entfernt wohnst.

- 110 €/Monat Lunch-Budget, 50 € Fitness-Zuschuss.

- 1.200 € jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget.

- Kostenlose Bücher: Buena zahlt jedes Buch, das du lesen möchtest.

Warum jetzt einsteigen 

- Du bist die Person vor Ort: Jede Verwaltung, die wir übernehmen, wird erst durch dich zu einem Buena-Betrieb. Ohne dich bleibt sie, was sie war.

- Wir wachsen schnell: Jeden Monat kommen neue Hausverwaltungen dazu. Deine Einsätze werden nicht weniger, sondern größer.

- Wir sind meritokratisch: Wer liefert, bekommt Verantwortung. Unser CEO war vor drei Jahren Junior Product Manager, unser COO vor zwei Jahren Chief of Staff.

- Wir verändern eine ganze Branche: Die deutsche Hausverwaltung läuft noch auf Papier und Excel. Du stellst das vor Ort um.

title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)
description:
New Challenge About Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do
Core engine development - Design and build the systems that power Hydris.
- Go is your primary language. You should be comfortable reading Rust and TypeScript across the codebase, even if you're not writing in them day-to-day.
- Own the architecture of a system that must run reliably on edge hardware, in disconnected mesh networks, and at scale — often all of that simultaneously.
Protocol and integration architecture - Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris.
- Make API design decisions that hold up across our client libraries without creating a maintenance burden.
- Continue refining the integration framework that lets Hydris connect to new sensor types, data sources, and command systems.
- Set the patterns for how built-in integrations (ADS-B, AIS, ASTERIX, Meshtastic, SpaceTrack, TAK, federation) are structured, tested, and maintained.
- Make it straightforward for external developers and system vendors to build their own plugins/integrations to Hydris.
Distributed systems - Architect the peer-to-peer mesh and federation layer that keeps Hydris operational in disconnected, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments.
- Solve the hard coordination problems: conflict resolution across federated nodes, eventual consistency of entity state, and track correlation across unreliable links.
- Ensure the system degrades gracefully rather than failing completely when connectivity is lost or constrained.
Technical leadership - Set technical standards for the codebase: how we test distributed behavior, how we handle protocol versioning, how we think about backward compatibility in an API-first product.
- Review code with a focus on long-term maintainability and operational correctness, not just feature completion.
- Make build-versus-integrate decisions and help the team clearly understand the trade-offs.

You should apply if you - Have built and shipped distributed systems that run in production, ideally in environments where reliability matters more than convenience.
- Are comfortable working across the stack, from Protobuf schema design and systems-level Go, to the TypeScript that puts a map in front of a user.
- Have well-formed views about API design and protocol evolution, informed by experience maintaining APIs that other people depend on.
- Can operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy but are adept at collaboration with colleagues toward high-quality technical decisions, at scale.
- Are interested in contributing to European military, maritime, and critical infrastructure defence systems.
- Write clearly and communicate architectural decisions in a way that survives beyond the conversation where they were made. 
- Working language is English. German is not required.
You'd be a great fit with - Experience with geospatial systems, sensor fusion, or track management.
- Familiarity with defense or ISR data standards like CoT/TAK, ASTERIX, SAPIENT, MIL-STD-2525.
- Background in networking, mesh architectures, or systems designed for contested or degraded communication environments.
- Experience working on developer-facing open-source infrastructure where adoption depends on the quality of the API and documentation.

We Offer - Remote work anywhere in Germany, or hybrid/on-site in Berlin or Munich if you're already based there and prefer an office.
- High degree of autonomy and ownership, a flat structure, and real input into technical direction.
- Annual €1500 Learning & development budget (available after probation).
